source.title: Error-aware Quantization through Noise Tempering
source.authors: Zheng Wang; Juncheng Billy Li; Shuhui Qu; Florian Metze; Emma Strubell

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper, including appendices and references.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports quantization accuracy and loss-landscape sharpness, but does not test any listed version: its sharpness measure is not the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7, and it does not measure training-test gaps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports generalization-related results for its quantization method. Its cited results about SGD, flat minima, and prior quantization methods are not rows. Hyperparameter values used in method setup are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates quantization noise tempering, reporting quantized-model accuracy and absolute-radius loss sharpness. It does not test any listed version. In particular, Section 5.1 uses an unscaled infinity-norm perturbation ball and reports neither training-test gaps nor comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures required by V7. General statements about batch size and optimizers are background, not experimental comparisons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their quantization-error-aware noise method improves uniform quantized-model accuracy and tends to yield flatter minima, which they interpret as favorable for generalization. They do not directly establish a relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and training-test gaps, and explicitly leave adaptive optimizers for further analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes quantization-aware training with learned step sizes and quantization-error-aware noise; it fine-tunes pretrained full-precision ResNets in quantized space. This is not the method used by any listed claim version.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise level c affects accuracy; the authors report that the best value varies by model-precision pair. Sharpness comparisons vary by precision and perturbation radius rho.

fits_no_version.finding: For selected CIFAR-100 ResNet-18 checkpoints at perturbation radius 0.001, noise tempering reduces sharpness from 6.09 to 4.97, 4.08 to 3.93, and 3.85 to 3.44 at 2, 4, and 8 bits.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization-error-aware noise tempering can reduce absolute-radius local loss sharpness in quantized ResNet-18 models.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected noise settings raise CIFAR-100 top-1 accuracy from 76.4% to 77.4% for 2-bit ResNet-18 and from 78.5% to 78.8% for 4-bit ResNet-50.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization-error-aware noise tempering can improve quantized classifier accuracy over LSQ for some model, precision, and noise settings.

record.problems: The sharpness experiment uses selected best-performing ResNet-18 checkpoints and does not report uncertainty. It measures a constrained-neighborhood loss sharpness score, not training-test gaps or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7. The reported accuracy comparisons do not include training accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Other precision and noise-level entries in Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5, as well as sharpness at rho 5.00E-04 in Table 3, are omitted to keep the record selective; they report quantized-model accuracy or sharpness but still do not measure a listed version's named outcome. The ImageNet accuracy table compares methods, but the source's flattened layout does not support assigning every displayed value to a method and precision with sufficient certainty.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out error, including interactions with dataset size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its relationship to training-test gaps among similarly fitted models, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match the supplied tables. The omitted sharpness and accuracy settings are declared in rows_left_out and do not test a listed version. The flatness claim attributed to the abstract in the record's excerpts actually appears in the Introduction's contribution list.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large-batch training and the effect of adapting the recipe.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, ranking of training-test gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting change in test accuracy.
